newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil police occupy drug war ravaged shantytowns.
newsitem.headline: Brazil police occupy drug war ravaged shantytowns.

text.p: Brazilian police were occupying two shantytowns on hills overlooking the famous Copacabana beachfront neighbourhood on Monday after a turf war between rival drug traffickers claimed nine lives in five days.
Many shops in the Cantagalo and Pavao-Pavaozinho favelas (shantytowns) remained closed and the streets were deserted as people stayed indoors.

"Several battalions of military and civil police have been deployed for an indefinite period of time in Cantagalo and Pavao-Pavaozinho to prevent further shoot-outs," said a police spokesman. "Today things are calm, but the shooting could start again any minute. We just don't know."

After months of relative calm in Rio's crime-infested shantytowns, violence flared up again when drug dealers from other shantytowns invaded the Cantagalo and Pavao-Pavaozinho favelas in the early hours of Thursday.

Five people, including a 14-year-old girl, died in ensuing gun battles which sent the favelas' inhabitants fleeing from their homes. Another four people were shot dead on Saturday during clashes with the police.
When traffickers set two houses alight in the early hours of Saturday, firemen were unable to enter the favela for several hours because of heavy gunfire.

A spokesman for Rio de Janeiro's state security department said police recovered 24 weapons, including submachine guns, AR-15 air rifles, grenades and other firearms of different calibres, during their operations in the favelas.
"This was the largest confiscation of arms during a single police operation in the state of Rio de Janeiro in the past year," the spokesman said.
Police also recovered 500 grams of cocaine.
The increasing use of ever more sophisticated weapons by drug traffickers is of growing concern to police who have confiscated 5,388 firearms this year in the state.
